title: Permutation signs and determinant definition
section: Determinants ▷ Permutations and the Defining Formula
terms: determinant; permutation; transposition; even permutation; odd permutation; sign of a permutation; Leibniz determinant formula.

exposition.text:

question.text:
A permutation matrix acts by a five-cycle on the first five coordinates and exchanges coordi-
nates 6 and 7. What is its determinant?
(A) −2 (B) −1 (C) 0 (D) 1 (E) 2

solution.text:
4
A five-cycle has sign (−1) = 1, while one transposition has sign −1. The product permuta-
tion has sign −1.

solution.text:
The column list (3, 1, 4, 2) has three inversions: (3, 1), (3, 2), (4, 2). Its permutation is odd,
so the coefficient is −1.

question.text:
In the polynomial expansion of the determinant of a general 4 × 4 matrix, what is the coefficient
of a a a a ?
11 23 33 44
(A) −2 (B) −1 (C) 0 (D) 1 (E) 2

solution.text:
Every determinant monomial must select each column exactly once. This product uses
column three twice and never uses column two, so it cannot arise from any permutation.
Its coefficient is zero, regardless of the sign of any proposed row ordering.
